Last month, after the TV tracking app TV Time shut down, one of its co-founders, Antonio Pinto, immediately announced the launch of a brand-new film and TV tracking app called Bingers, emphasising its social features. Here are the relevant details.

Bingers is now available for download

The film and TV tracking app TV Time was previously announced by Whip Media to be shutting down. One of its co-founders immediately announced the launch of Bingers, positioning it as a "fast, beautiful and fun community-driven watch list".

According to TechCrunch, Bingers is now available for download on iOS and Android platforms, offering a "spiritual successor" for users still searching for a TV Time replacement — TV Time was once one of the most popular TV tracking apps globally.

Users who were previously TV Time users and saved their data via the export tool provided by the platform before the app shut down can import their archives into Bingers, continuing to use the service seamlessly; as for users who never exported their data, or new users who have never used a TV tracking app, they can start from scratch to build their own viewing records.

Bingers strongly emphasises its community-driven features, such as user profiles, comments, episode ratings, GIF animations, polls, and character popularity elections. Pinto told TechCrunch that these features are precisely what made TV Time endure over time:

For users who simply want to track the shows and movies they have watched, Bingers offers dedicated watch lists and viewing records. Similar to TV Time, the app also displays upcoming programme schedules and premiere dates, counting down how many days until broadcast.

Bingers is available for free download on the App Store and currently does not offer any in-app purchases.
